issues.description: The problem specification (and UML) requires a parameterless method checkOrderReady(): void, but the solution implements checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) and calls it with a boolean argument from orderMeal. This mismatches the specified method signature and would confuse students about the expected API (and tests that expect a parameterless method).
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a parameterless checkOrderReady() method consistent with the problem statement/UML. Either remove the boolean parameter from the existing method, or add an overload public void checkOrderReady() that delegates to checkOrderReady(true/false) so the API matches the specification and students/tests can call the parameterless method.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and requirements) specifies a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void, but the solution implements checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) and calls it with a boolean argument. This changes the expected method signature and parameterization for the same conceptual operation (checking and serving ready orders). Students reading the problem would implement a no-arg checkOrderReady(), so the boolean parameter in the solution creates a mismatch and potential confusion about the required API.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the no-argument signature expected by the problem: implement public void checkOrderReady() and, if internal logging is needed, have the no-arg method delegate to a private helper (e.g., private void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)) or use an internal flag. This keeps the public API aligned with the problem statement while preserving optional logging behavior.
